facts.a: 85 to 150. The 15 unscored pretest questions are mixed in and you can't tell which they are.
Up to 5 hours, including tutorial and optional breaks.
3 scored case studies, 6 questions each, following one patient.
Not bad news! It stops when it's 95% confident you're above or below the passing line.
Yes. Many Next Gen items give partial credit (e.g. SATA, matrix).
Pass / fail only. Official results come from the regulator.

judgment.example: You notice: SpO₂ 88%, RR 28, HR 118, sudden chest pain, anxiety, and right calf was swollen yesterday. Skill: picking the important findings out of a long chart, often with a highlight question.
Post-op immobility + calf swelling + sudden dyspnea + tachycardia → links to pulmonary embolism, not just anxiety or pain. Skill: connecting findings to conditions.
Possible PE vs. pneumonia vs. anxiety. PE is life-threatening right now, so it ranks first. Skill: ranking problems by urgency.
Goals: improve oxygenation and prevent clot growth. Plan: raise HOB, give oxygen, prepare for anticoagulation and CT angiography. Skill: choosing the right interventions and avoiding wrong ones.
Apply oxygen, call a rapid response / notify the provider (SBAR), start the IV, give heparin as prescribed. Skill: what to do first, often a drag-and-drop or matrix.
SpO₂ now 95%, RR 20, less anxious → improving. If not, escalate. Skill: judging whether the patient got better, often a trend question.

demo.stem: Which value is a normal adult serum potassium?

types.name: Select all (SATA)
types.desc: Choose every correct option. Could be 1 or all of them. Partial credit applies.

demo.stem: Which are signs of hypoglycemia? Select all that apply.
demo.rationale: Fruity breath and warm dry skin point to hyperglycemia/DKA. Remember: 'Cold & clammy, need some candy.'

types.name: Matrix
types.desc: A grid. For each row pick the right column (e.g. Indicated / Not indicated).

demo.stem: Client with pneumonia: mark each action.
demo.rationale: Elevate the HOB, encourage coughing and deep breathing, and encourage fluids to thin secretions.

types.name: Highlight
types.desc: Tap the findings in a nurse's note that need follow-up.

types.name: Drop-down (cloze)
types.desc: Complete a sentence by choosing from drop-down lists.

types.name: Bowtie
types.desc: Middle = the condition; left = 2 actions to take; right = 2 parameters to monitor.

types.name: Drag & drop / ordering
types.desc: Put steps in order or place options into categories.

types.name: Trend
types.desc: Look at data across several times (vitals, labs) and decide what changed.

priority.detail: A new problem beats a long-standing one.
A real problem now beats a risk.
…unless the client is in danger: then act first.
RN: assess, teach, evaluate, unstable clients. UCP: routine tasks for stable clients.
Try the least restrictive safe option first.

examDay.title: Arrive 30 min early
examDay.hint: Bring the exact ID registered with Pearson VUE

examDay.title: Check-in
examDay.hint: Palm vein scan, photo, signature. Belongings go in a locker

examDay.title: Tutorial
examDay.hint: Short tutorial on the item types (you'll already know them!)

examDay.title: Exam begins
examDay.hint: No going back to previous questions

examDay.title: Optional breaks
examDay.hint: Raise a hand. Break time counts toward the 5 hours

examDay.title: Exam ends
examDay.hint: Can stop anywhere from 85 to 150 questions. Don't read anything into it!

examDay.title: Results
examDay.hint: Official result from the regulator. Unofficial 'quick results' may be available for a fee in some places
